paper_metadata.title: Hybrid Quantum Classical Model for Enhanced Cross Border Financial Fraud Detection

experiments.description: Comparative quantum-classical fraud detection experiment using a classical SVM baseline versus a QSVM on a cross-border financial transaction dataset; the quantum side uses angle encoding, entangling gates, and a precomputed quantum kernel, evaluated on a simulator.

algorithm.variant: QSVM with angle encoding and quantum kernel evaluation

problem_formulation.encoding_details: Each preprocessed feature is mapped to a rotation angle on a qubit; the paper states a feature vector x=[x1,...,xn] is mapped onto an n-qubit circuit, with each feature controlling an Ry rotation. Features are normalized to [0, π] before encoding.
problem_formulation.objective_function: Binary classification of transactions into Genuine (0) vs Fraud (1) using a quantum kernel-based SVM.

problem_instance.description: Cross-border financial fraud detection on a financial transaction dataset with transaction-level features including amount, country risk, time of day, sender blacklisted status, sender age in days, and label.

dataset_specification.description: Columns listed: Transaction ID, Amount, Country Risk, Time of Day, Sender Blacklisted, Sender Age Days, Label. Time of Day is encoded from Day/Night to 0/1. PCA reduces the feature space to at most four components. The paper does not report train/test split or total dataset size.

problem_instance.data_preprocessing_details: Data validation for required columns; feature encoding of Time of Day from categorical to numerical 0/1; filtering by Time of Day, Country Risk, Amount, Sender Age Days, and Sender Blacklisted; standardization to mean 0 and standard deviation 1; PCA to a maximum of four components; feature normalization to [0, π] for quantum gates.
problem_instance.evaluation_methodology: Performance compared using accuracy, precision, recall, F1-score, false positive rate, ROC curves, confusion matrices, and AUC; the paper does not report cross-validation or number of runs.

implementation_details.classical_preprocessing: Data validation, categorical encoding, filtering, standardization, PCA, and feature normalization.
implementation_details.classical_postprocessing: Prediction evaluation via accuracy, precision, recall, F1-score, false positive rate, ROC/AUC, and confusion matrix analysis.

speedup_claims.conditions: The paper discusses potential quantum advantages qualitatively, but does not report a measured runtime or asymptotic speedup for this experiment.
speedup_claims.caveats: No numerical speedup, runtime, or complexity comparison is reported.
